title: Whole Turkey (frozen)

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 2.6. No events, price changes, or promotions are planned. The TikTok trend is noted but lacks evidence of past impact or measurable lift. The classical uplift model suggests +66% based on Halloween, but that event is week-before, not in the target week. Past Halloween effects are noisy and noise-adjusted to x1.66, but this week is 2 weeks after. No recent promotion or price change. The model's suggestion is not directly applicable. No driver justifies a multiplier >1.0. The noise-adjusted effect of the TikTok trend is unconfirmed. No evidence of demand shift. The baseline uncertainty is already well-calibrated.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 2.6 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 14.7 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 8.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-122% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
